newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn, soy harvest seen slowed by rain, cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn, soy harvest seen slowed by rain, cold.

text.p: Rain and cold temperatures are likely to slow the progress of corn and soybean harvests in the U.S. Midwest over the next few days, meteorologists said.

"The first three days of the week were nearly ideal for harvesting and they (farmers) could have got a lot done. But beginning yesterday (Thursday) and looking into next week it doesn't look very good," agricultural meteorologist Joel Burgio of Weather Services Corp said.
The next rain-bearing front will reach the western Corn Belt late Sunday and move through the main regions Monday and Tuesday bringing 0.25 to 1.00 inch of precipitation, he said.

Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc, said in the last 24 hours, Illinois and Indiana had 0.25 to 1.50 inches of rain with 70 percent coverage, while Ohio had 0.10 to 0.75 inch with 50 percent coverage.
Further west it was drier, although in Sioux City, Iowa there was 0.01 inches and in southern Minnesota rainfall of a few hundredths of an inch was reported, he noted.

Gesser said that Hurricane Lili had slowed the current front down, increasing the amount of rainfall. The next front, due Monday into Tuesday, should move faster and bring just a trace to 0.50 inch of precipitation to the Corn Belt, Gesser added.
Gesser said he also expects rain-bearing fronts moving through the U.S. Midwest on Thursday and Friday next week and then again on the following Sunday and Monday .
"The frequency suggests light precipitation," he said.
Gesser forecast temperatures would be below normal for the period and precipitation to be normal to above normal.
Burgio, of Weather Services Corp saw highs in the upper 40s (degrees Fahrenheit) to mid 50s F early next week and lows in the 20s to low 30s F.
"It will definitely be a lot cooler and wetter than the first part of this week," he said.
